Attachments are not downsized server-side by this PR, so this can bypass or confuse enforcement of attachment size limits."

If the configured limit or the web server limit differs, users receive an incorrect error message, making upload failures confusing and harder to diagnose."

      "title": "API URL downloads are capped at 10 MB for all upload types, ignoring configured limits",
      "body": "FileHelper.download now always allows 10 MB, regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb or attachment size limits. For images the PR attempts to downsize afterward, but for non-image attachments there is no downsizing step. This can permit or attempt uploads larger than admin-configured limits and increases resource usage by downloading oversized remote files."

      "category": "data",
      "title": "Downsizing rewrites the same open Tempfile in place",
      "body": "OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path as input and output for an external image tool while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. If the tool truncates, replaces, or renames the output file, the open file descriptor can point at stale data, so tempfile.size and later Upload.create_for may read the wrong bytes or an old inode. A failed conversion can also corrupt the only copy of the upload. Write to a separate temporary file and replace tempfile only after a successful conversion."
    },

      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Downsizing loop can stop while the image is still too large or conversion failed",
      "body": "The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and ignores the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails or five attempts are insufficient, execution still proceeds to Upload.create_for with a file that may exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The controller should verify the final size and return an error if it cannot reduce the file enough, rather than relying on later behavior."
    },

      "title": "Duplicate downsize method definition silently removes width/height API",
      "body": "Ruby does not support method overloading. The second self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 overrides the previous self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145. The older width/height variant is dead code, and any existing caller using separate width and height arguments will now pass the height argument as opts, likely causing TypeError or wrong behavior. Remove the dead method or use a distinct method name if both signatures are needed."
    },

      "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",

      "title": "Image processing command is executed via string interpolation without escaping",
      "body": "convert_with runs a shell command built from instructions.join(' ') using backticks. Paths are inserted as unquoted, unescaped arguments. The new automatic downsizing passes temporary file paths to this code; if a path contains spaces or shell metacharacters, the command can fail or execute unintended commands. Use system with an argument array or Shellwords.escape instead of interpolating into a shell string."
    }

findings.title: Client-side upload size validation is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile previously used Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the limit depended on whether the upload was an image or attachment and on admin settings. The change replaces this with a constant 10 MB. Users can now select attachments or images larger than the configured limit (up to 10 MB), and the displayed 'file too large' error reports 10 MB even when the forum limit is lower or higher. Attachments are not downsized server-side by this PR, so this can bypass or confuse enforcement of attachment size limits.

findings.title: 413 upload error message uses hardcoded limit instead of site setting
findings.body: When the server or web server returns HTTP 413, the alert now always says the maximum size is 10 MB. The previous code used Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb. If the configured limit or the web server limit differs, users receive an incorrect error message, making upload failures confusing and harder to diagnose.

findings.title: API URL downloads are capped at 10 MB for all upload types, ignoring configured limits
findings.body: FileHelper.download now always allows 10 MB, regardless of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb or attachment size limits. For images the PR attempts to downsize afterward, but for non-image attachments there is no downsizing step. This can permit or attempt uploads larger than admin-configured limits and increases resource usage by downloading oversized remote files.

findings.title: Downsizing rewrites the same open Tempfile in place
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...) uses the same path as input and output for an external image tool while the Ruby tempfile object remains open. If the tool truncates, replaces, or renames the output file, the open file descriptor can point at stale data, so tempfile.size and later Upload.create_for may read the wrong bytes or an old inode. A failed conversion can also corrupt the only copy of the upload. Write to a separate temporary file and replace tempfile only after a successful conversion.

findings.title: Downsizing loop can stop while the image is still too large or conversion failed
findings.body: The loop makes at most five 80% resize attempts and ignores the boolean returned by OptimizedImage.downsize. If conversion fails or five attempts are insufficient, execution still proceeds to Upload.create_for with a file that may exceed SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. The controller should verify the final size and return an error if it cannot reduce the file enough, rather than relying on later behavior.

findings.title: Duplicate downsize method definition silently removes width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not support method overloading. The second self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) at line 149 overrides the previous self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) at line 145. The older width/height variant is dead code, and any existing caller using separate width and height arguments will now pass the height argument as opts, likely causing TypeError or wrong behavior. Remove the dead method or use a distinct method name if both signatures are needed.

findings.title: Image processing command is executed via string interpolation without escaping
findings.body: convert_with runs a shell command built from instructions.join(' ') using backticks. Paths are inserted as unquoted, unescaped arguments. The new automatic downsizing passes temporary file paths to this code; if a path contains spaces or shell metacharacters, the command can fail or execute unintended commands. Use system with an argument array or Shellwords.escape instead of interpolating into a shell string.
